_note: M-LOADOUT PerkCatalog (docs/spec/loadout.md §1.2, docs/perk-design.md). A perk is the third slot of a player's kit (A14, 2026-09-04: beside the weapons; the ALT-button accessibility switch moved OUT of this slot in S50 -- see `easy_reload` below). v1 perks are PASSIVE: pure head-frame tweaks the compiler already knows how to write ($PSET armor/shield, $AMMO + $WEAP ammo/reload tokens, a $SIR key swap) or, for `motion_tracker`/`second_wind`, entirely NODE-LOCAL (the phone's own logic against its own gun; `effects: {}` on purpose -- do not invent a wire lever for either). `mechanism: slot_frame` rows would be a $WEAP in slot 1 whose effect lives in the VICTIM's $SIR table (game-wide, not per-player) — they stay `hidden` until the emit-side bench proves them. `verified` = effect proven on hardware. Copy is player-facing: no protocol jargon. S50 (2026-09-17, perk balance pass, decided in docs/perk-design.md §2): every perk now trades on the SAME lever its opposite buys, so the set is rock/paper/scissors instead of a ladder. `effects.max_armor_add` is a FLAT armour grant/cost, `compile.py`'s `_MAX_ARMOR_ADD` table (keyed by perk_id) is the one place the compiled arithmetic runs -- this field is the wire-visible documentation of the same number, kept a plain integer because `app/src/hud/hud.js` and `webapp/mc/src/screens/Kit.tsx` both render it literally as '+N ARMOR'. body_armor is +25 (was a flat +50, S50's 'straight upgrade' finding -- 'maybe 50 is too much armor and it should be 25', Tony 2026-09-17); quick_switch is -20, floored at 0 and capped at 255 by `compile.armed_armor`/`armed_shield`. In a game whose base armour is 0 (the Shields preset), body_armor's grant compiles into the SHIELD ceiling instead of armour (`compile.is_shields_preset`). `hidden` (2026-09-18): `motion_tracker` and `second_wind` are the two NODE-LOCAL perks of the S50 set (docs/perk-design.md §2). The compiler has nothing to write for either, and the phone half is not built, so they are hidden until it is. A visible perk that does nothing is worse than a missing one: a player picks it, gets nothing, and reports a bug in something else.

perks.name: Body Armor
perks.desc: Start every life with 25 extra armor, about a fifth more health pool. Armor soaks hits before your health does. The rig is heavier though: your reload takes a quarter longer.

perks.name: Extended Mags
perks.desc: Double the magazine and double the reserve on your primary. Fewer reloads, longer fights, more rounds to burn -- but the bulkier magazine slows your draw: switching to your other weapon takes 30% longer.

perks.name: Quick Hands
perks.desc: Reload in half the time. Your primary is back in the fight before theirs is -- the trade is a lighter magazine, 20% fewer rounds carried.

perks.name: Quick Switch
perks.desc: Draw your second weapon in half the time: the gun's swap delay drops from 0.85 s to 0.43 s. A lighter rig means less padding though -- 20 less armor.

perks.name: Armor Piercing
perks.desc: Your primary ignores armor and shields and goes straight to health. The rounds are heavier: fewer of them, and the gun cycles slower. Against a bare target a normal weapon still kills faster, and against an armored or shielded one this wins. It fits any plain-damage primary; the host is told if the chosen weapon cannot carry it.

perks.name: Motion Tracker
perks.desc: Nearby enemies show on your HUD, no direction, refreshed every few seconds. You carry information instead of firepower -- anyone who accepts being seen can still shoot first.

perks.name: Second Wind
perks.desc: Once a life, the hit that would finish you leaves you standing instead. It costs nothing up front, because it only pays when you are already losing -- and a weapon that kills in one hit goes through it anyway.

perks.name: Med Kit
perks.desc: A healing shot for teammates — tag an ally to top up their health.

perks.name: Concussion
perks.desc: A stun burst that jams an enemy's weapon for a few seconds.
